verdict: Yes, if you can compete on design and safety rather than price. Channapatna toys have a GI tag, import curbs have pushed parents toward Indian-made toys, and artisans sell well below retail prices. What holds brands back is safety compliance, slow handmade production and parents comparing prices with mass-produced toys.
angle: Channapatna, about 60 km from Bengaluru, has made lacquered wooden toys for generations, traditionally from soft ivory wood with natural colours. The cluster has skilled makers but few brands that bring new designs to them. A founder who co-designs learning toys for today's parents (stacking, sorting, early maths) with safety test reports in hand has a real gap to fill, both online and with preschools.

faq.q: How much does it cost to start a Channapatna toys business?
faq.a: Buying from artisan workshops and selling online can start at ₹75,000–3 lakh, covering design work, first stock, safety tests, packaging and marketing.

faq.q: Do wooden toys need BIS certification?
faq.a: Toys sold in India fall under the Toys Quality Control Order and generally need BIS certification. Some handmade toys from registered artisans are exempt, so check whether your artisans and products qualify before you list online.
